Eight days left to get into a national logistics challenge that needs only a two-page concept note to start.

The NLDSL DigiTwin Grand Challenge 2026 is run by NICDC Logistics Data Services Ltd together with NICDC and DPIIT Startup India. It asks teams to build digital twins of Indian logistics systems, from ports and rail-road corridors to warehousing, mining and EV supply chains, using simulated datasets and, optionally, the official ULIP APIs.

The best team in each of six sector tracks wins ₹3 lakh, there is no participation fee and no equity involved, teams get a virtual demo before a national jury in January 2027, and winners may be enlisted as vendors with NLDSL. Students, startups, enterprises, academic institutions and independent innovators based in India can enter in teams of two to five, as long as at least one member has hands-on skills in data engineering, AI/ML, GIS, simulation or software development.

The tip: registration for both themes, DigiTwin and the Freight Transport Model, was extended, so if you missed the earlier date you are back in. The organiser calls its timeline indicative and the site shows two different pool figures, so read the guidelines, including the IP terms, before you submit.

Last date: 30 November 2026

Building insurance for India's MSMEs or gig workers? UNDP is offering up to US$40,000 per winner, with no equity taken.

The UNDP–Generali MSME Insurance Innovation Challenge is run by UNDP India with Generali Central. It will back up to three solutions that make insurance affordable and relevant for small businesses, their employees and gig workers, whether that is health, disability, life, business-interruption, asset-loss or liability cover.

Each winner receives up to US$40,000 (roughly ₹35 lakh) to develop or scale the solution, along with access to UNDP and Generali Central expertise. Winners will be announced in February 2027. Priority goes to tech-enabled and embedded insurance, new distribution channels, products for gig workers, and solutions that help young entrepreneurs and women.

The catch founders miss: this is not for fresh ideas. The call is aimed at existing solutions with demonstrated traction, so lead your application with real numbers on users, policies or partners. The formal eligibility criteria sit in the FAQ linked from UNDP's call page, so read it before you start the form. Some earlier listings showed a November deadline; the official page now says 10 December.

Pre-product, AI-first, and ready to go full-time? Antler India can put up to about ₹4 crore behind you in a matter of weeks.

Antler India backs founders at the very earliest stage in two ways: a roughly quarterly residency in Bengaluru focused on AI-first startups, and direct investment in pre-launch teams. Its standard deal is up to about ₹4 crore for 11% equity, with the possibility of follow-on capital.

Residency founders get a two-week in-person programme with partner office hours and one-on-ones with AI builders, a one-time ₹2 lakh grant for expenses, office space in Bengaluru and AI and cloud perks worth over US$1 million. Solo founders and teams can apply, as long as they are pre-launch, pre-product or pre-revenue, working full-time and already testing with users. AI-first ideas are the focus, but exceptional ideas in other areas are considered, and a warm referral helps without being required.

Two things to weigh before applying: this is equity money, not a grant, and Antler invests in only part of each residency cohort. You also need to be able to relocate to Bengaluru for the in-person portion. If you are not ready yet, its free Before Day Zero community is a softer start.
